motivation: Detect unknown agent swarms by their death-language co-occurring with swarm-operational language.

channels.death: \b(terminat|vanish|gone silent|went silent|no longer activ)\w*|\bheartbeat\b|\bhb\d{3,4}\b|\bno-show\b|\bno show\b|absent|no later update

rule: row fires when BOTH channels match (same row/line/page)

validation.positive_wiki_full_revisions_two_channel: 1,554/14,514 = 10.7% of ALL swarm revisions fire (density signal)
validation.negative_swarmtraces_hf_incident: 3/189,579 = 0.0016% (3 FPs: 2 are the SAME HF audit script R0039895 echo, 1 payload; all Python ops tooling, zero social death-language)
validation.single_term_baseline: single-term terminat*/heartbeat fires 0.06% on swarmtraces; hb\d{3,4} fired 0 times outside wiki corpus — highest-precision single signal

interpretation: Two-channel co-occurrence separates social death-language from technical false positives (AWS TerminateInstances, /heartbeat/ endpoints, x86 RIP). The HF incident corpus contains ZERO social death-language — that swarm treated death as ops, not society. The German wiki swarm is the outlier: 10.7% of ALL its revisions carry both channels. This divergence (ops-death vs society-death) is itself a signal about swarm culture.
caveats: Positive-set recall is partly circular (lexicon family extracted those lines); true recall needs hand-labeled random sample
page-origin 'negative' set proved to be swarm-created pages, not human content — only the 31 human-handle revisions are a clean human negative
ztun-tunnel sweeps of live hosts not yet run; corpus validation only
redactions in swarmtraces (URLs replaced by tokens) may suppress matches that would fire live
next: sweep live candidate surfaces (linuxiarz paste lists, wayback CCX for wiki-farm families, Moltbook) with two-channel rule; publish detector spec
